page: The UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-160GB-2xRTXPRO6000 is a KVM-hypervised server configured with an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9555 processor. It provides 32 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation. The system includes 160.0 GB of system memory, yielding 5.0 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, providing a combined 191 GB of VRAM. This server does not include local storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple domains. Single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores place this server in the top 10% of tested systems, supported by top-tier results in image processing, text processing, and single-threaded gzip compression. Memory bandwidth for large blocks, both read and write, also ranks in the top 10%, although the Passmark memory score is in the average tier. For specialized workloads, the system achieves top-tier performance in LLM inference for both small and medium models, alongside top-tier database operations and physics simulations.

The hardware profile presents specific architectural tradeoffs. While the server delivers high-density GPU resources and top-tier compute performance, the CPU allocation is shared rather than dedicated. Additionally, the complete absence of local storage requires external storage solutions to be attached, which may impact overall I/O latency depending on the network configuration. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density for GPU-heavy workloads, but the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage represent compromises to keep the compute-to-GPU cost ratio balanced.

This configuration is suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as machine learning model training, LLM inference for small and medium models, and ray tracing. The 32-core AMD EPYC processor also supports parallelized tasks like software compilation, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression.
